title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Eight years ago, Anne Elliot let her family talk her out of the man she loved. Now Captain Wentworth is back, richer, prouder and coldly polite. She must sit across the room and watch him look at other women.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Emma Woodhouse has arranged one marriage already and thinks she has a gift. So she picks a husband for her shy friend Harriet, and every sign she reads is wrong. Only Mr Knightley dares to tell her so.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Elinor Dashwood hides every feeling, and her sister Marianne hides none. After their father dies, the two leave their home with almost no money. Then each falls in love, and each man has a secret.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
blurb: Jane Eyre is ten when her aunt locks her in a dark red room. Years later, as a governess at Thornfield Hall, she hears a strange laugh on the top floor at night. Mr Rochester says it is only a servant.

title: North and South
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
blurb: Margaret Hale grew up among green fields, and the smoky mill town of Milton feels like another world. John Thornton, its proudest owner, thinks she looks down on him, and he may be right. Then a strike begins.

title: Anne of Green Gables
author: L. M. Montgomery
blurb: Matthew Cuthbert goes to the station to fetch an orphan boy and comes home with a red-haired girl who never stops talking. Marilla wants to send her back. Anne has other plans, and plenty of mistakes still to make.

title: Far from the Madding Crowd
author: Thomas Hardy
blurb: Bathsheba Everdene turns down the shepherd who loves her, then inherits a farm and runs it alone. One careless joke, a valentine sent for fun, brings a rich farmer to her door. A soldier with a sword is waiting in the woods.

title: The Age of Innocence
author: Edith Wharton
blurb: Newland Archer is about to announce his engagement to the perfect bride when her scandalous cousin, Countess Olenska, appears in the opera box. In a society that never says what it means, he begins to want what he must not have.

title: Cyrano de Bergerac
author: Edmond Rostand
blurb: Cyrano can fight a duel and make up a poem at the same time, but he is sure no woman could love his nose. His cousin Roxane loves a handsome soldier with no words. Cyrano has plenty, and he lends them.

title: The Rival at Desk Four
author: The Hating Game
blurb: Ines Marlow has the best desk in the tram office, until a humming stranger takes the one opposite. Jonah Pike drinks tea from a chipped blue mug and fixes her printer. Eight weeks, one job, one winner.

title: Just Pretending
author: The Love Hypothesis
blurb: Wren Ashby has one second to stop her aunt's matchmaking, so she points at the nearest man in the café. Kit, the ferry mechanic, plays along. Their rules fit on a napkin. Their feelings do not.

title: Two Keys, One Door
author: The Flatshare
blurb: Odile opens her new flat and finds a stranger inside, holding a key to the same door. The agent booked it twice, and nothing else is free for a month. One violin, one microphone, one strip of tape.

title: Summer at Willow Bay
author: People We Meet on Vacation
blurb: Nora Bell has come to Willow Bay to sign some papers and leave. Instead she finds five leaking boats, a note from her late aunt asking her to stay one summer, and a quiet boat builder next door.

title: The Runaway Prince
author: Red, White & Royal Blue
blurb: Days before his engagement is announced, Prince Felix climbs onto a night train in a borrowed coat and calls himself Fen. By morning he is working in a lakeside bookshop, very badly, for a bookseller who has no idea who he is.

title: Letters I Never Sent
author: The Notebook
blurb: Behind a stuck drawer in an old desk, Iris finds thirty letters written in 1961 and never posted. She takes the train to the seaside town on every envelope. Someone there never forgot, and Iris has unsent words of her own.

title: Every July
author: One Day
blurb: At nineteen, Nell and Sam sit on a wooden jetty and promise to meet there every July. Then come other people, a ship at sea and a summer when only one of them turns up. How long can a promise last?

title: The Duke's Convenient Bride
author: The Duke and I
blurb: A duke must marry within a year or lose his land to a cousin who would sell every farm. Hester, a farmer's daughter quick with numbers, needs money to save her family. Her contract has three rules, and one is the truth.

title: Snowed In at Cedar Lodge
author: The Unhoneymooners
blurb: A snowstorm has closed the only road to Cedar Lodge, and its newest guest is not who she says she is. Poppy is a secret inspector. Four days of burnt soup, burst pipes and Cal's kindness make her notes harder to write.

title: The Grumpy Baker of Maple Street
author: Book Lovers
blurb: Jonas Reed has one rule in his bakery: no talking before the first bread. Hazel Quinn, a cheerful bookkeeper, talks to everyone. She has one month to fix his books, and a rival bakery is about to open across the street.

title: A Wedding to Survive
author: The Wedding Date
blurb: Lena Costa has a long list and one job: a perfect wedding. Then the flowers go to the wrong farm, a goat eats the list, and best man Theo Hart proves good at fixing things. A storm is coming.

title: The Love Letter Café
author: P.S. I Love You
blurb: In a seaside café, a wall of forty drawers holds letters that people are too afraid to send. Nina Alvarez has come to sell the place, but finds twelve letters her grandmother wanted posted, and Eli, the postman she never wrote to.

title: A Study in Scarlet
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: One word, written in blood, is all the dead man leaves behind on the wall. A stranger named Sherlock Holmes reads the empty house like a book, and his new friend Dr Watson learns how far back a murder can reach.

title: The Sign of the Four
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: Every year a pearl arrives in the post for Mary Morstan, and no one will say who sends it. Her father vanished long ago. Holmes and Watson follow a clever little dog and a fast boat after a stolen fortune.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: A king in a mask, a club for red-haired men, a goose with a jewel inside, a bedroom where a girl hears a whistle at night. Twelve cases come to 221B Baker Street, and Holmes sees what everyone else misses.

title: The Moonstone
author: Wilkie Collins
blurb: On Rachel Verinder's birthday, a yellow diamond is locked in a cabinet. By morning it is gone, and the only clue is a smear on a wet door. Three strangers watch the house, and a famous detective arrives to find the thief.

title: The Woman in White
author: Wilkie Collins
blurb: A hand touches Walter Hartright's arm on a dark road at midnight. It belongs to a woman dressed all in white, and she is running from someone. Soon a smiling count with pet white mice begins to plan something terrible.

title: The Murders in the Rue Morgue
author: Edgar Allan Poe
blurb: Two women are dead in a locked room in Paris, and the police can find no way in or out. Every witness heard a strange voice, but no two agree what language it spoke. Auguste Dupin trusts the evidence.

title: The Innocence of Father Brown
author: G. K. Chesterton
blurb: Father Brown looks harmless. He is short and shabby, with a round face and a clumsy umbrella. But the master thief Flambeau cannot fool him, and one by one the strangest crimes in England start to make sense.

title: The Mystery of the Yellow Room
author: Gaston Leroux
blurb: A woman is attacked in a room with one locked door, one barred window and no chimney. Yet the attacker has vanished. Eighteen-year-old reporter Joseph Rouletabille says the answer is simple, if you take the puzzle by the right end.

title: Arsène Lupin, Gentleman-Burglar
author: Maurice Leblanc
blurb: A wireless message warns a ship full of passengers that the famous thief Arsène Lupin is on board. But which of them is he? In nine adventures, this charming gentleman-burglar robs the rich and makes Inspector Ganimard look foolish.

title: The Thirty-Nine Steps
author: John Buchan
blurb: Richard Hannay has a dead neighbour in his flat, a notebook full of code and strangers watching his door. The police will blame him. So he borrows a milkman's coat and runs for Scotland, with a spy gang close behind.

title: Eight Guests, One Storm
author: And Then There Were None
blurb: Orla Venn goes down to the cellar for one special bottle of wine and never comes back. When the lights fail, her guests find the door bolted from outside. The sea has cut off the island, and the killer is here.

title: The Counselor's Last Session
author: The Silent Patient
blurb: Daniel Reeve has said almost nothing in eight months of sessions. On Marianne Cole's last day, he says his sister did not fall, hands her a brass key and walks out. She promised to keep his secrets. Should she break that promise?

title: The Wife Who Vanished
author: Gone Girl
blurb: Isla Marlowe's phone rings in a kitchen drawer and her supper goes cold. Her workshop clock has stopped at twenty to ten, and the town whispers about her husband. Her sister Hannah remembers a childhood game, and starts looking for a clue.

title: Murder at Maple Court
author: The Thursday Murder Club
blurb: Four retired friends meet every Wednesday for tea and old crimes. Then the man who wants to sell their garden is found dead in a locked glasshouse, and one alibi mentions a train that Walter, the retired signalman, knows was not running.

title: The Cipher Beneath the Bridge
author: The Da Vinci Code
blurb: Ines Varga is paid to call an old iron bridge unsafe. But the iron is sound, and beneath it she finds twelve plates of letters that make no words. The man who hired her wants the bridge gone.

title: The Hacker With the Red Scarf
author: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
blurb: Two hundred thousand pounds has vanished from a charity that buys breakfasts for children, and the police think the kind old treasurer took it. Tamsin Rook, a hacker who only breaks in when invited, thinks someone borrowed his name.

title: Neighbours Who Know Too Much
author: Big Little Lies
blurb: Gerald Pike watches every house on Larkspur Close and writes down what he sees. The morning after the Midsummer party, he is dead at the foot of his garden steps. New neighbour Priya Nair, a court interpreter, starts to listen.

title: The Housekeeper's Notebook
author: The Maid
blurb: Ada Brennan writes down every small thing she notices while she cleans, even the time. On the night Leopold Ashgrove turns eighty, he dies in his library chair, and the police look first at his housekeeper. Her green notebook may help.

title: Window Seat, Platform Nine
author: The Girl on the Train
blurb: At 7:42 every morning the train stops for a minute beside a garden, and a woman in a yellow coat waves. Then one day she hangs washing with the wrong hand and does not wave. Only Mina, a secretly jobless bookkeeper, notices.

title: The Lawyer in the Back Seat
author: The Lincoln Lawyer
blurb: Where to, boss? Nico Barrow can barely see after dark, so he works from the back seat of a black cab. His new client is a bike courier accused of stealing a priceless violin, and he swears he only delivered a case.

title: The Sixth-Form Detective
author: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
blurb: Seventeen-year-old Zee Rahman picks a school project question the town has forgotten. Years ago, charity money vanished from a school safe and a caretaker took the blame. As she digs, one polite man never asks what she has found.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
blurb: Dorothy's farmhouse lands on a witch, and the dead witch's silver shoes end up on Dorothy's feet. Now she must follow the yellow road to a Wizard who might send her home. His price is another witch's life.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: Dinner is cold and the host is late. Then he limps in, pale and bruised, and says he has just come back from the year 802,701. What he saw there is still waiting, deep underground.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: The metal thing in the pit on Horsell Common is too hot to touch, and then its top begins to turn. Within days, Martian machines taller than houses are burning Surrey. One ordinary writer must survive.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
blurb: On a dreary November night, Victor Frankenstein's creation opens its eye, and Victor runs away. Alone, hungry and nameless, the Creature learns about people by watching them through a window. Then he comes looking for his maker, with a demand.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
blurb: The Count is a perfect host, but every door in his castle is locked, and he casts no reflection in the mirror. Jonathan Harker escapes. Then the Count sails for England, and Jonathan, Mina and a few friends must stop him.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
author: Jules Verne
blurb: Something huge is sinking ships in the dark, and nobody knows what it is. Professor Aronnax sails out to hunt it. The monster is a steel ship, and its captain, Nemo, says no guest may ever leave.

title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
blurb: A coded note falls out of an old book, and only hunger helps young Axel read it. It says there is a way into the centre of the Earth, through a volcano in Iceland. His uncle, the Professor, starts packing.

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
blurb: Mole is so tired of spring cleaning that he drops his brush and walks out into the sunshine. By evening he has found a river, a best friend called Rat, and a rich, boastful neighbour, Toad, whose newest craze is motor cars.

title: The Jungle Book
author: Rudyard Kipling
blurb: Shere Khan the tiger wants the human baby that crawled into the wolves' cave, but Mother Wolf will not give him up. The boy, Mowgli, grows up with a bear and a panther as teachers. The tiger is patient.

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
blurb: Mr Utterson hears about a small, pale man who tramples a child and walks on, and about a door nobody likes to discuss. The man is Hyde, and he has a strange hold on Utterson's old friend, Dr Jekyll.

title: The Academy Under the Mountain
author: Harry Potter
blurb: Every lamp Wren Tallow lights hums to her, very softly. Then a kind stranger offers her a place at a school hidden inside a mountain. There the lamps are starting to fail, and the answer lies far below the Ninth Stair.

title: The Last Lantern of Aldermoor
author: The Lord of the Rings
blurb: An old man falls asleep at Corin's ferry and does not wake, leaving a glowing lantern in the boy's hands. Outside, a grey fog wipes out the memory of everyone it touches. Corin must carry the light to the Beacon at Cairnhead.

title: The Reluctant Burglar's Map
author: The Hobbit
blurb: Ilse Quill locks her door at sunset, mends old maps and likes her tea hot. Then a sea captain brings a thief's torn chart and a plan: steal the one map that could save a hungry island. Only Ilse can read it.

title: Crowns of Salt and Ash
author: A Game of Thrones
blurb: King Edric's will names no heir, only a test: keep salt and ash at peace for a year and a day. His youngest daughter Sera sees that the letters pushing both sides toward war are forged. Who is writing them?

title: The Water Merchant's Daughter
author: Dune
blurb: In Oshenar, even a spoonful of water is counted, and Ysra Vell counts better than anyone. When the Deep Well starts to fall and her father rides away, she follows him across the Glass Desert. Someone is stealing the river.

title: Arena of Dust
author: The Hunger Games
blurb: Ilka's name is called, and she is sent into the Bowl, a desert arena with one jar of water and nine days. But she is a water-finder, and she soon sees that every dry channel points to the Tower.

title: The Boy Who Won the Simulation
author: Ender's Game
blurb: A boy from a seaweed farm breaks the record at a tide game, and a stern commander comes to his door. Her Academy trains young pilots. Kofi wins every test, but nobody warns him about the last one.

title: Survival Log, Day One
author: The Martian
blurb: Joon-ho Park wakes to static. A solar flare has knocked out his radio, his crew has lifted off without him, and everyone thinks he is gone. He has one sealed base, one weak air filter and one stubborn plan: stay alive.

title: The Signal From Tau Lyra
author: Project Hail Mary
blurb: In the dead of night in the Chilean desert, a radio astronomer hears a pattern in the static, repeating again and again. Soon telescopes across the world hear it too. The first words they can read say: please answer.

title: Neon Rain City
author: Neuromancer
blurb: Juno Vale mends umbrellas in the endless rain, and she has not touched a keyboard in years. Once she was the best data thief in the city. Then a cheeky twelve-year-old courier brings her a glass key that hums near water.

title: A Traveller's Guide to Nowhere
author: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
blurb: The most careful accountant in Bristol is standing on his doormat in his slippers when a rude, talking book tells him his holiday has begun. Oswin never booked one. Now he needs three stamps, one form and a very long way home.

title: One Small Step a Day
author: Atomic Habits
blurb: Priya's New Year list of big goals lasts until February. Then her neighbour Sam hands her a cup of tea and a smaller idea, one step so small it feels silly. Can a minute a day really change a life?

title: Focus Without the Noise
author: Deep Work
blurb: Noor ends every busy day with a screen full of open tabs and nothing important finished. Her calm colleague Hana goes home on time. Hana's secret is simple, one protected block of time for one task, and the phone in another room.

title: Do Less, Do It Well
author: Essentialism
blurb: Rosa's restaurant has five dishes on the menu, and she cooks every one with care. Lena's life has no menu. She says yes to everything and she is worn out. Rosa shows her how to choose and say no kindly.

title: Hard Task First
author: Eat That Frog
blurb: Noor's list has one job that frightens her, so she does everything else first. The dread only grows. Then she turns the list upside down, with a timer, a sticky note and a small, kind rule for the morning.

title: A Clear Head, A Clear Day
author: Getting Things Done
blurb: Amara cannot sleep, because her head is full of things she must not forget. One evening she sits down with a pen and a large blank sheet and writes down all of it. A simple system turns the pile into calm.

title: Your First Hour
author: The Miracle Morning
blurb: Mei snoozes, scrolls in the dark and starts every day already behind. Kofi works nights, and Elena has a toddler. None of them needs a perfect routine, only a short, realistic first hour that fits a real life.

title: The Learning Mind
author: Mindset
blurb: Maya buys a battered guitar and tells herself she has no talent. Her teacher Ines, in a small room above a bakery, says everyone starts badly. Over one year Maya learns what practice does to the brain, and what mistakes are for.

title: Keep Going
author: Grit
blurb: Ben wants to row on Mill Lake in a boat he built himself. The excitement lasts four weeks. Then come a plank cut too short, a new baby, and a neighbour who says the boat will never float.

title: Stronger Than You Think
author: Can't Hurt Me
blurb: Dara leaves the office with her things in a box and feels she has nothing left. Her neighbour Hugo, a retired firefighter, asks her to do one small hard thing every day. A charity ten-kilometre run is twelve weeks away.

title: Decide Your Direction
author: Awaken the Giant Within
blurb: Sail sixty miles one degree off course and you miss your harbour by about a mile. Leon, thirty-three and stuck, has been off course for years. His aunt Rosa, a ferry captain, asks him one question at a time.

title: Goals That Stick
author: Think and Grow Rich
blurb: Kofi has wanted to make pottery for years, and nothing has happened. His neighbour Ana, a retired mountain guide, says a wish with no date is only a wish. So he sets one. Twenty mugs, sold by the end of June.

title: Here and Now
author: The Power of Now
blurb: Elise misses her stop because her mind is already in tomorrow. Behind a green gate she finds Yusuf, an old gardener who draws three circles in the soil, for past, future and here. By autumn, she knows the way into the third.

title: Choose What Matters
author: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
blurb: Your attention is a small bag of coins, and Maya spends hers on every email, opinion and plan. She is exhausted. This short, honest guide helps you choose the few things worth the struggle, and let the rest go.

title: Purpose in Hard Times
author: Man's Search for Meaning
blurb: A job of twenty-five years ends for Ruth, floodwater covers Omar's fields, and Lena's mother is seriously ill at home. None of them can undo it. Each finds something small to hold on to, and a reason to take the next step.

title: A Reason to Get Up
author: Ikigai
blurb: At nine o'clock Grace holds an empty mug in her quiet kitchen. After a lifetime of teaching, she has nowhere to be. Kofi works nights and loses his free hours to his phone. Both find small, real reasons to start the day.

title: Four Simple Rules for Life
author: The Four Agreements
blurb: Ada, a retired ferry captain, writes four rules on four white cards for her neighbour Leo. He runs a bicycle shop and says yes too quickly. The first rule is to mean what you say. The other three are just as simple.

title: Quiet Confidence
author: Ego Is the Enemy
blurb: Sam is the new head of sound at the Orchard Theatre, and he talks too much because he wants to look brilliant. Helen, a stage manager there for thirty years, shows him a quiet confidence that needs no audience.

title: Free From Other People's Opinions
author: The Courage to Be Disliked
blurb: At midnight Lina is still finishing other people's work. She says yes to everyone and no to herself. Her aunt Rosa, a tailor, shows her two gardens, one holding her own choices and one holding what everyone else thinks.

title: How to Get Along With Anyone
author: How to Win Friends and Influence People
blurb: Nora starts at Fennel Street Bakery before sunrise, hoping everyone will like her. The head baker is gruff, one customer is rude and the driver is always late. Priya, the manager, gets along with nearly everyone, and Nora wants to know how.

title: Live by Your Principles
author: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
blurb: Ines repairs bicycles all day and still feels she is rushing, never steering. On her wall hangs her grandfather's brass compass. Then a big chain shop opens nearby and makes her an offer, and she must decide what she stands for.

title: Worry Less, Live More
author: How to Stop Worrying and Start Living
blurb: A head full of what-ifs keeps Elif awake. Her neighbour Mrs Hale, who has sore knees and worries of her own, hands her a trowel. Worries grow like weeds, and Elif learns to clear them one row at a time.

title: As a Man Thinketh
author: James Allen
blurb: Plant useful seeds in your mind, says James Allen, or weeds will grow there on their own. His short book from 1903 follows that one idea into character, goals and peace, and it still asks sharp questions of its reader.

title: Self-Reliance
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
blurb: Everyone around you wants you to fit in. In an essay from 1841, Ralph Waldo Emerson says the opposite. Trust yourself, stop copying other people and do your own work, because nothing else can bring you peace.

title: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day
author: Arnold Bennett
blurb: Each morning your purse is filled with twenty-four fresh hours, whoever you are. You cannot borrow from tomorrow, and nobody can take today. Arnold Bennett's cheerful 1908 guide shows busy people how to spend them well.

title: The Science of Getting Rich
author: Wallace D. Wattles
blurb: In 1910 a writer claimed that getting rich follows laws, like arithmetic. Some of Wallace Wattles's advice is sensible, and some is pure belief. This retelling keeps his boldest ideas and tells you honestly which is which.

title: Acres of Diamonds
author: Russell H. Conwell
blurb: Ali Hafed sells his farm and sets out to find diamonds. Back home, the man who bought it leads his camel to the garden stream. Russell Conwell told this tale thousands of times, to ask where your own chances hide.

title: The Way to Wealth
author: Benjamin Franklin
blurb: The crowd at the sale is angry about heavy taxes, and everyone wants old Father Abraham to speak. His answer is a string of sharp little sayings about time, debt and idle hands. Benjamin Franklin wrote it, and it still stings.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
blurb: The best general never has to fight. That is the strange claim of a book written about 2,500 years ago in China and credited to Sun Tzu. It says to win first, through planning, timing and knowing yourself and your rival.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
blurb: In 1513 a Florentine official lost his job when the Medici family came back, and wrote a handbook for rulers on his farm. Machiavelli's advice on winning and keeping power still shocks readers. Is it honest, or a warning?

title: Your Money, Your Rules
author: Rich Dad Poor Dad and The Psychology of Money
blurb: Priya is twenty-four, and her first full pay has just arrived. Her neighbour Mr Okafor, a retired shopkeeper, offers her one idea each week for a year. By the end she has money rules of her own, written for her own life.

title: Assets and Liabilities in Plain Words
author: Rich Dad Poor Dad
blurb: Leila's pay vanishes every month, and she cannot say where it goes. Over ginger tea, a retired shopkeeper gives her one question that sorts everything she owns or owes into two groups. Even a car needs a closer look.

title: How Money Really Works
author: The Psychology of Money and The Intelligent Investor
blurb: Same job, same pay, same start. Ten years on, Ana and Ben are in very different places, and clever tricks are not the reason. Their story shows how saving, patience, luck and fear shape money.

title: Start Investing Today
author: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
blurb: Mira is twenty-eight, has some savings and a card bill, and has never bought a share. Her cousin Dev, who once sold in a panic and regretted it, shows her what shares, bonds and index funds are, and why costs matter.

title: The Index Fund Way
author: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
blurb: Ben has a hot tip about one company, and he cannot explain why its price will keep rising. His friend Leila, with her first savings, asks a retired bank clerk instead. Mr Hale shows her low fees and plain funds.

title: Small Savings, Big Future
author: The Millionaire Next Door
blurb: Amara drives a bus, Joel bakes bread, and their money is gone before the month ends. Aunt Wen, who has saved quietly all her life, asks them to write down every purchase for a month. The diary is full of small leaks.

title: One Simple Plan for Wealth
author: The Simple Path to Wealth
blurb: Marta delivers parcels all day and lies awake at night worrying about money. She decides to write one plan on a single sheet, with a few clear steps, and to keep to it for ten years. It is simple enough to copy.

title: Build It Lean
author: The Lean Startup
blurb: A drill used twice is a waste, thinks Mira, and she imagines a street where neighbours lend each other tools. Her friend Kofi asks one hard question: what if nobody wants it? Mira learns to test the idea with small, cheap experiments.

title: Build Something New
author: Zero to One
blurb: Every day at Eastgate market, good vegetables spoil in the heat. Ravi, a young engineer, wonders why nobody has fixed it. He sketches a cold box that runs on sunlight, and learns why one small market comes before a big one.

title: How Strong Companies Last
author: Good to Great
blurb: Brightwell Paper has outlived louder, richer rivals, and it is seventy years old. Tilda, its new manager, wants to know how. Every Friday the retired boss, Mr Okafor, answers her questions about what lets a company last.

title: Lead Through the Hard Days
author: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
blurb: In one week, Kofi loses a customer worth a third of his income. He has forty workers and ten blue vans, and no idea what to tell them. Over Friday coffee, a retired manager helps him tell the truth.

title: Work Less, Earn Smart
author: The 4-Hour Workweek
blurb: Sixty hours a week, and Leo still feels behind. His friend Dina runs a workshop and works only four days. Over a year, she helps him measure results instead of hours, say no and charge what his work is worth.

title: Lead With Purpose
author: Start With Why
blurb: Sofia's bakery is busy, yet something feels empty, and a cheaper rival has just opened nearby. A retired sea captain tells her that a business without purpose is a ship with an engine and no compass. Sofia must find hers.

title: Negotiate Without Fighting
author: Never Split the Difference
blurb: A landlord, a boss, a shop assistant, a sister: you will probably negotiate with one of them this week. This short guide shows how to prepare, listen and ask better questions, so you stay calm and keep the relationship.

title: Why People Buy
author: Influence
blurb: Rosa's Corner bakes good bread, yet some people walk straight past. Rosa learns what really moves a buyer: feelings first, then trust, fear of a bad choice and the power of a story. She learns to persuade without being unfair.

title: Teach Yourself to Be Wealthy
author: I Will Teach You to Be Rich
blurb: Nina's first full pay has arrived, and she has no plan for it. Her friend Kofi, a year ahead with money, gives her four jars: bills, savings, investing and fun. Step by step, she learns what to do with each one.

title: The Dhammapada
author: Buddhist scripture (traditional)
blurb: Suffering follows a troubled mind, says an old verse, the way a cart wheel follows the ox. The Dhammapada gathers short sayings linked to the Buddha on anger, habit and peace, each one small enough to carry through your day.

title: Tao Te Ching
author: Laozi
blurb: Legend says a border guard begged an old sage to write down his wisdom before he left China. What he left were eighty-one short poems about water, silence and a strength that does not push. Short enough to read in an evening.

title: The Bhagavad Gita
author: Hindu scripture (traditional)
blurb: Arjuna drops his bow. Two armies wait, and he cannot fight the cousins and teachers he loves. His charioteer, Krishna, answers with a conversation about duty, fear and who we really are, at the heart of one of India's most loved texts.

title: The Sermon on the Mount
author: Gospel of Matthew
blurb: A teacher sits on a hillside above the Sea of Galilee, and the crowd leans in. He calls the gentle and the peacemakers blessed, then speaks of anger, money, worry and trust. These are the words of Jesus in Matthew's Gospel.

title: The Book of Proverbs
author: Hebrew Bible
blurb: Go and watch an ant, says one old saying, and learn how to work. The Book of Proverbs holds ancient Israel's short, sharp advice on money, friends, words and temper, and a wisdom that calls out loudly in the market square.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
blurb: The most powerful man in the Roman world writes to himself before dawn: you could leave this life at any moment, so act well now. Marcus Aurelius wrote these notes for himself, and they read like honest advice from a friend.

title: The Prophet
author: Kahlil Gibran
blurb: After twelve years in Orphalese, a man waits for the ship that will take him home. Before he sails, the people ask him to speak of love, work, pain and death. Kahlil Gibran's poems have comforted readers for a century.

title: The Analects of Confucius
author: Confucius
blurb: A teacher with a few students and one big idea: that anyone can become a better person. Confucius spoke simply about learning, family, honesty and kindness, and his students wrote it all down. Meet him through short sayings and small, human stories.

title: The Enchiridion
author: Epictetus
blurb: Epictetus was born a slave, tradition says, yet he taught that no one can take your inner freedom. His Enchiridion is a short handbook on what you control, what you do not, and how to stay calm either way.

title: Be Here, Be Calm
author: Wherever You Go, There You Are
blurb: Maya burns her toast while checking her phone, then realises she remembers nothing of the bus ride. A Thursday evening class in the community hall gives her six weeks of small, honest practice for being where she actually is.

title: The Mind That Watches
author: The Untethered Soul
blurb: Ines cannot stop her thoughts, so she takes a summer job at a tiny railway station. The old stationmaster asks her one odd question: who hears the voice in your head? Slowly she learns to watch her thoughts pass like trains.

title: Walk Slowly, Breathe Deeply
author: The Miracle of Mindfulness
blurb: Hana walked fast for a living, and now that she has retired she still cannot slow down. Then she meets Samir, who strolls the river path at a snail's pace. Beside him she learns to breathe as if each breath were new.

title: Staying Calm When Life Breaks
author: When Things Fall Apart
blurb: In one grey week Noor loses her job, and her father is rushed to hospital. The old ferry captain next door never tells her what to believe. He offers small, simple practices from many traditions for staying steady when everything breaks.

title: Radical Kindness to Yourself
author: Radical Acceptance
blurb: Elena makes one small mistake at work, and a cruel voice in her head will not stop. Her aunt invites her to a Thursday circle in the library, where she learns, step by step, how to be on her own side.

title: What Joy Really Is
author: The Book of Joy
blurb: Ravi turns thirty-five with a cake, a good job and no feeling at all. He packs a notebook and spends a month on trains, asking bakers, nuns and gardeners one question: what is joy, and how do you let it in?

title: A Purpose Bigger Than You
author: The Purpose Driven Life
blurb: Nadia owns a small bakery and still wonders what her life is for. So do a bus driver, a cleaner, a retired engineer and a teenager. Together they find that purpose grows when it reaches beyond yourself, with or without faith.

title: Life as a Seeker
author: Autobiography of a Yogi
blurb: A girl on a harbour wall asks questions that nobody around her can answer. Grown up, Ines sits in silence with monks and meditators and shares bread with strangers. She learns that seeking is a way of living, not a place.

title: The Last Lessons of a Teacher
author: Tuesdays with Morrie
blurb: A handwritten letter from her old primary-school teacher says she is dying and would like to see her. Priya, an architect always in a hurry, starts visiting every Saturday, and under a pear tree she learns what a good life needs.

title: Letting Go of the Ego
author: A New Earth
blurb: Leila wins the meeting, wins the argument, and goes home feeling empty. Over one summer in a harbour boatyard, a retired boat builder helps her hear the proud, defensive voice inside her, and hold it more lightly.

title: Stillness for Beginners
author: Be Here Now
blurb: Seventeen-year-old Eli arrives at his grandmother's farm in January with a buzzing phone and a head full of noise. Ruth does not lecture. She sits by the window at dawn, doing nothing, and says stillness is a skill he can learn.

title: Forgiveness, Step by Step
author: The Book of Forgiving
blurb: Three years ago Nell's brother sold their late father's café without telling her, and she has not spoken to him since. Over one spring, a retired teacher walks beside her through the slow, honest steps of forgiving.

title: A Calm and Happy Life
author: The Art of Happiness
blurb: Ravi has a good shop, a nice home and a restless mind. Lena, a hospital nurse, is always rushed. Through their small changes, this short book shares simple ideas that many wisdom traditions agree on, and practices you can try today.

title: Walking
author: Henry David Thoreau
blurb: Four hours a day, no destination, no hurry. Thoreau called it sauntering, and he said he could not stay healthy or cheerful without it. Follow his short essay into the swamps and see why he trusted the wild.

title: Eat More Plants
author: How Not to Die
blurb: A retired dietitian with a vegetable patch has one rule for his neighbour Lena. A link is not proof. Over one year she learns to cook more plants, one simple meal at a time, and to question the headlines.

title: The Long Life Plan
author: Outlive
blurb: Omar is fifty-two, and his sister Salma, a physiotherapist, hates hype. Once a month for a year they climb the stone steps of Bell Hill, and she explains what really helps people stay strong and independent as they age.

title: Hormones and Hunger, Explained
author: The Obesity Code
blurb: Noor bakes bread all day, yet by four o'clock she is starving. Her neighbour Ines, a retired nurse, explains the signals between stomach and brain, and says plainly what science does not know. There is no blame and no quick fix.

title: Sleep Is Your Superpower
author: Why We Sleep
blurb: Lena is still studying at three in the morning, with an exam in two weeks. Her aunt Rosa, a sleep technician, shows her what the brain does at night and why sleep may beat one more late hour.

title: Breathe Better, Feel Better
author: Breath
blurb: Before every concert, Iris's heart races and her breath turns quick and high. Her friend Dev, a lung physiotherapist, explains the nose, the lungs and the diaphragm, and is honest about which breathing claims are stronger than the evidence.

title: Run Like a Kid Again
author: Born to Run
blurb: Joy is eight and runs everywhere for fun. Her father Sam, forty-two, cannot sprint a few steps without gasping. With a patient coach and a walk-run plan, he starts slowly, with one small town fun run in sight.

title: Exercise for a Sharper Mind
author: Spark
blurb: Leila forgot a colleague's name today, and her keys again. Her nephew Ravi, a neuroscience student, takes her on daily walks along the canal and explains what exercise may do for memory, focus and mood, and what it cannot do.

title: Where People Live Longest
author: The Blue Zones
blurb: Nina is almost ninety and still walks to the market every morning. Her granddaughter Elena, a data analyst, wants to know why. She follows the maps and numbers behind long lives, and sorts luck from place from choice.

title: Foods That Protect You
author: Eat to Beat Disease
blurb: Amara is fourteen, and her science project has one rule. Show the evidence. With her grandfather Kofi, a retired cook, she tests the big claims about food and builds a plate of everyday foods that may help the body look after itself.

title: Feed Your Gut
author: Fiber Fueled
blurb: Noah lives on quick meals eaten on a bicycle, and a crowd of tiny microbes in his gut eats them too. His neighbour Ines studies microbes. She shows him how everyday food feeds them, and how much science still does not know.

title: Steady Energy All Day
author: Good Energy
blurb: Every day at three, Hana's energy vanishes, and coffee and a biscuit do not fix it. Her colleague Dev, a part-time running coach, helps her test sleep, light, meals and movement, and tells her what is proven and what is not.

title: Why Healthy Food Feels So Hard
author: The Hungry Brain
blurb: Noor planned a healthy dinner, and by ten o'clock she was eating biscuits. Her uncle Idris, a retired dietitian, never blames her. He explains old hunger signals, clever food and busy lives, and helps her try small, kind changes.

title: Lift Heavy, Start Simple
author: Starting Strength
blurb: Out of breath on the stairs at forty-four, Kofi walks into a gym for the first time. His coach Ana teaches him a few basic movements, from the squat to the carry, and shows him how to add weight slowly and safely.

title: Ten Moves for a Lifetime
author: Built to Move
blurb: Grace, sixty-three, trips on a kerb. She is not hurt, but she is frightened. Her neighbour Mateo, a physiotherapist, teaches her ten everyday moves, from walking to getting up off the floor, and how to practise each one safely.

title: The Stress Reset
author: Why Zebras Don't Get Ulcers
blurb: Ravi teaches all day and lies awake at night, with a body like an alarm nobody can switch off. Over one busy week he learns what stress does inside us, then tries calming tools that have real evidence behind them.

title: A Better Night, Starting Tonight
author: The Sleep Revolution
blurb: It is midnight, then one, then two, and an accountant named Lena is still awake, counting the hours she will lose. Over two weeks she learns how sleep works and tries small changes, from morning light to a calmer last hour.

title: Why Moving Makes You Happy
author: The Joy of Movement
blurb: Priya walks for fifteen minutes at lunchtime, and her mood lifts. She wants to know why. Over three months she builds a habit and learns what movement does for mood and mind, even for people who dislike exercise.

title: Stay Strong Past Fifty
author: Younger Next Year
blurb: Marta wants to keep up with her five-year-old grandson, but one day she cannot get up from the lawn without help. Her neighbour Sam, a physiotherapist, shows her how to look after muscles, bones and balance, one small step at a time.

title: Twelve Rules for a Sharper Brain
author: Brain Rules
blurb: One bad day, Teo forgets a colleague's name and his own card code. Every Sunday evening, his friend Ada, a psychology teacher, shares a rule about sleep, attention, memory or calm. Each rests on real research, and she never promises too much.

title: Real Food, Simple Rules
author: In Defense of Food
blurb: Every headline tells Elif something different, and tonight she is eating takeaway again. Her uncle Davit, a cook for forty years, gives her simple rules for shopping, cooking and eating, with no diet and no guilt.

title: Work Hard, Rest Well
author: Peak Performance
blurb: Two designers have the same job. Ravi never rests. Marta rests on purpose. This short guide follows them to show how effort and recovery work together, from sleep and breaks to easy days, and when long tiredness needs a doctor.

title: The Histories
author: Herodotus
blurb: A rich king asks a wise visitor who the happiest man is, expecting to hear his own name. The answer is a warning. Herodotus follows kings and oracles to the Persian wars, with Marathon, a bridge of boats and three hundred Spartans.

title: The Gallic War
author: Julius Caesar
blurb: Caesar builds a wall around a city, then a second wall facing outward, because a huge army of Gauls is coming to rescue it. Before Alesia come a bridge over the Rhine and two landings in Britain, all told by Caesar himself.

title: Plutarch's Lives
author: Plutarch
blurb: A boy lifts a rock and finds his father's sword and sandals beneath it. Plutarch tells the lives of Greeks and Romans, from Theseus to Cleopatra's golden barge, and shows how small stories reveal a person's character.

title: The Travels of Marco Polo
author: Marco Polo
blurb: At seventeen, Marco Polo leaves Venice for a court so far away that the road takes years. There he sees paper money, black stones that burn and a Great Khan who likes him. Back home, some people refuse to believe his stories.

title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
author: Frederick Douglass
blurb: Frederick Douglass never knew his birthday, and he was told that learning to read would spoil him as a slave. He learned anyway. This is his own account, naming real people and places, of how he fought back and got free.

title: Up From Slavery
author: Booker T. Washington
blurb: A penniless teenager arrives at a school and is told to sweep a room. He cleans it three times. Booker T. Washington, born a slave, tells how that test led to Tuskegee, a school he began with no land and no building.

title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
author: Benjamin Franklin
blurb: A dirty, tired seventeen-year-old walks into Philadelphia with almost no money, buys three rolls and is laughed at by a girl who will become his wife. Benjamin Franklin tells the rest himself, from his thirteen virtues to the clubs he founded.

title: Twelve Years a Slave
author: Solomon Northup
blurb: Two strangers praise Solomon Northup's violin and offer him paid work. He is a free man from New York. Then he wakes in chains. It will take twelve years, and one honest carpenter, to bring him home.

title: How Humans Took Over the World
author: Sapiens
blurb: Neanderthals, Denisovans and our own species once shared the world, and now only one is left. This book follows the story of Homo sapiens, from the first stone tools to the Moon and a world of eight billion people.

title: Why Some Countries Got Rich First
author: Guns, Germs, and Steel
blurb: A thousand years ago the great cities were not in Europe. So why did a few countries get rich first? Historians point to place, rules and chance, and each gets a fair hearing, from the first farms to the first factories.

title: The Roads That Built the World
author: The Silk Roads
blurb: Over three million years ago, someone walked across soft volcanic ash and left a line of footprints. It may be the first road. Follow the routes that came next, carrying silk, gold and ideas, to the cables on the sea floor.

title: Rome in Ten Moments
author: SPQR
blurb: In legend, sacred geese wake the defenders of a hill at night, just as the Gauls begin to climb. It is one of ten moments, from a wolf and twins to the last western emperor, that show how Rome rose and fell.

title: The Horseback Empire
author: Genghis Khan and the Making of the Modern World
blurb: When Temujin's father is poisoned, his clan walks away and leaves the family in poverty. In 1206 the boy is named Genghis Khan, and his riders go on to reach from China to Poland. Here is how, and at what cost.

title: The Americas Before Columbus
blurb: In 1491 the Americas were not empty. Tens of millions of people lived there, from Mexica city builders to Inca relay runners. Meet them, and see how many foods on your plate, like maize, potatoes and chocolate, began with them.

title: The Salt Trade That Shaped Nations
author: Salt: A World History
blurb: In 1930 Gandhi walked nearly four hundred kilometres to the sea to pick up a handful of salt, and mass protest followed. Why? Follow salt from desert caravans and Roman roads to hated taxes, and see how it shaped wars and freedom.

title: Thirty Days to World War
author: The Guns of August
blurb: A driver takes a wrong turn in Sarajevo and stops near a young man with a gun. Within weeks, a promise from Berlin and a deadline for Serbia turn a crisis into a war much bigger than most leaders wanted.

title: The Rules History Keeps Repeating
author: The Lessons of History
blurb: Roman emperors mixed cheap metal into their silver coins. In 1923 German money became almost worthless. Twelve patterns, from stretched empires to bursting bubbles, show how history rhymes, and what the past can and cannot tell us.

title: How Maps Shape Power
author: Prisoners of Geography
blurb: Cyril Radcliffe, who had never visited India, was given about five weeks to draw the border between India and Pakistan. Every map is a choice like that. Learn how rivers, mountains and mapmakers shape power, and how to read any map.

title: London Under the Bombs
author: The Splendid and the Vile
blurb: When the sirens sound, thousands of Londoners go down into the Underground to sleep on bunks, drink tea and sing. For 57 nights in a row in 1940, bombs fall above them. This is how ordinary people lived, worked and kept going.

title: The Rise of the Plains Warriors
author: Empire of the Summer Moon
blurb: Horses had vanished from North America for ten thousand years when the Spanish brought them back. Soon the Comanche, once a mountain people on foot, dominated the southern Plains from the saddle. Then came war, loss and survival.

title: Europe in One Evening
author: The Shortest History of Europe
blurb: Forty thousand years ago, someone in Europe painted on a cave wall. It takes fifty short scenes to get from there to the Berlin Wall and the European Union, with Greeks, Romans, plague, printing and revolutions on the way.

title: Lincoln and His Rivals
author: Team of Rivals
blurb: A man from a log cabin beats better-known rivals for his party's nomination, then asks them to sit at his table. Abraham Lincoln builds a cabinet of proud, strong men as the country splits, and has to make them work together.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: For twenty years Charles Darwin quietly collected facts. Then a letter from Alfred Russel Wallace arrived with the same idea, and he rushed to write. Here is the book that argues nature, not a breeder, picks who survives.

title: The Voyage of the Beagle
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: At twenty-two, Charles Darwin took a place on a small survey ship and did not see home for almost five years. He crossed the Andes, felt an earthquake and met giant tortoises. Come along and watch him begin to wonder.

title: The Chemical History of a Candle
author: Michael Faraday
blurb: Blow out a candle and hold a flame to the rising vapour, and the fire jumps down and relights the wick. Michael Faraday did this for children, then used one candle to explain water, air and even your own breathing.

title: Relativity: The Special and General Theory
author: Albert Einstein
blurb: Two people watch two lightning bolts strike a railway track and disagree about whether they struck together. Einstein says both are right. His own short book takes you on to bent starlight and curved space, in plain words.

title: Experiments on Plant Hybridisation
author: Gregor Mendel
blurb: A monk spent about eight years in a garden counting peas, and the numbers kept landing near three to one. Gregor Mendel's own paper shows how he found a hidden rule of inheritance, and how it lay forgotten until 1900.

title: The Story of Everything, Short
author: A Brief History of Time
blurb: Look up from a dark hilltop and you are looking into the past. In fifty short steps, this book follows the story back to the Big Bang and forward to the far future, and says plainly what nobody knows yet.

title: A Tour of the Universe
author: Cosmos
blurb: An imaginary glass lift waits on a dark rooftop. Noor says it can go as fast as she wishes, and Kit steps in. They pass the Moon, the planets and a black hole, then reach the edge of what we can see.

title: Why Genes Behave Like They Do
author: The Selfish Gene
blurb: Maya finds a box of handwritten recipe cards in her grandmother's bakery, and her uncle says every living thing has one. Over one summer, he shows her how genes are copied, why mistakes happen, and why genes are not puppet strings.

title: The Universe in an Afternoon
author: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
blurb: On a hot Sunday, Anya asks her uncle Ravi what the universe really is. He has a chalkboard, a teapot and five hours to answer. By six o'clock, the board is full of her own questions.

title: Everything You Missed in School
author: A Short History of Nearly Everything
blurb: The Moon probably began when a planet-sized object crashed into the young Earth. School may have skipped that part, and much more. Fifty short steps take you from the Big Bang to your own brain, and never talk down to you.

title: Strings, Space and Time
author: The Elegant Universe
blurb: Our two best theories of nature work brilliantly, yet they clash inside a black hole. String theory is a bold, unproven idea about tiny vibrating loops that might bring them together. It says plainly what we know and what we do not.

title: Physics in Six Ideas
author: Six Easy Pieces
blurb: One ordinary day, twelve-year-old Kofi rides his bike, watches a kettle boil and looks at the stars, and his Aunt Zainab, a physics teacher, shows him the six big ideas behind all of it.

title: How Genes Shape Who We Are
author: The Gene
blurb: Noor has her grandmother's curls and her father's green eyes, and she wants to know why. Her aunt Amara, a scientist, explains the tiny instructions inside every cell, from peas and twins to gene editing, and what they cannot decide.

title: The Fish Inside You
author: Your Inner Fish
blurb: Kofi has a bad case of hiccups in a museum, and a fossil scientist says even hiccups have a story. As they walk, he learns that his jaw, ear bones and hands trace back to ancient fish.

title: Think Like a Scientist
author: The Demon-Haunted World
blurb: Dev says his lucky socks help his team win. His friend Ines asks how they could know. At the school Question Club, they learn to test ideas fairly, spot how we fool ourselves and say I might be wrong.

title: Physics, One Idea at a Time
author: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
blurb: In 1971 an astronaut dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon, and they landed together. Start there and take physics one idea at a time, through energy, atoms, bent space and the puzzles nobody has solved.

title: Why Time Feels Like It Flows
author: The Order of Time
blurb: Clocks in orbit tick faster than yours, and an hour in your head can fly or crawl. This book follows time through sundials, Einstein, the arrow that breaks eggs and the brain, and admits that nobody fully understands it.

title: A Tour Through Your Body
author: The Body
blurb: Your heart beats about a hundred thousand times a day, and you never have to think about it. This guided tour of the body you live in runs from skin and bones to the brain, the gut and the cells.

title: The Secret World of Fungi
author: Entangled Life
blurb: After rain, a mushroom pushes up through the leaves, and it is only the fruit of something much larger hidden in the ground. Fungi recycle dead wood, trade with trees, make bread rise, and most kinds have never been named.

title: Earth Seen From Space
author: Pale Blue Dot
blurb: Ana watches about sixteen sunrises a day from a window on the space station, and her niece Lila has asked her to describe everything. Hurricanes, reefs and auroras glide past, and a thin blue line of air keeps everything alive.

title: Ten Questions About the Universe
author: Brief Answers to the Big Questions
blurb: The part of the universe we can see is about ninety-three billion light-years wide, and nobody knows what lies beyond it. Ten honest questions follow, from how the universe began to whether we are alone, and where the answers run out.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
blurb: A stranger caught in a snowstorm sleeps in a room where the name Catherine is scratched everywhere, and something taps at the window. The housekeeper tells him why: a homeless boy, a wild girl and a revenge that lasts a lifetime.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
blurb: Jo March will do almost anything for her family, even sell her hair. With her sisters Meg, Beth and Amy she grows up poor and close in a small house, each with her own dream, while Father is away at war.

title: Romeo and Juliet
author: William Shakespeare
blurb: Juliet kisses a stranger at her father's party, and only afterwards learns that he is a Montague, her family's sworn enemy. By the next day they are secretly married. In Verona, one fight in the street can ruin everything.

title: Mansfield Park
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Fanny Price is ten when she is sent to live with rich relatives, and she grows up as the least important person in the house. When the charming Crawfords arrive from London, everyone is dazzled. Only Fanny sees where it leads.

title: Northanger Abbey
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Catherine Morland has read so many ghost stories that she expects a secret behind every door. At Northanger Abbey she finds a black cabinet in her room and a host whose wife died years ago. She is sure there is a crime.

title: The Lady of the Camellias
author: Alexandre Dumas fils
blurb: Marguerite Gautier wears white camellias twenty-five days a month and red ones for the other five, and nobody in Paris knows why. When a poor young man truly loves her, she dares to dream of a quiet life, until his father calls.

title: The Bookshop on Lantern Lane
author: The Bookshop on the Corner
blurb: Tessa Marlowe plans to sell her late great-uncle's crooked bookshop within a week. Then a note falls out of a book, written for a stranger. There are many more, and a quiet carpenter who lights the lane's lamps every evening.

title: Midnight at the Lighthouse Inn
author: The Notebook
blurb: Every midnight, Iris climbs her lighthouse to check a lamp that has never gone dark. Then an engineer arrives on the last ferry, sent to decide whether it should be switched off for good. He is hiding something about that light.

title: The Valley of Fear
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: A secret message names a house in Sussex and the man who lives there. Soon he is dead in his study, with a card reading V V 341 beside him. Holmes knows the neat story told to the police is false.

title: The Memoirs of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: A dog does nothing in the night. A face appears at a cottage window. A racehorse vanishes from the moor. In eleven cases Dr Watson shows Holmes at his best, until a Swiss waterfall and the one man he truly fears.

title: The Return of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: For three years Watson believed his friend was dead. Then an old book collector turns up in his study and takes off his disguise. Thirteen cases follow, with dancing men, six plaster Napoleons and a blackmailer in a fine house.

title: The Purloined Letter
author: Edgar Allan Poe
blurb: A letter has been stolen from a royal lady's room, and she could not stop it. For months the police have searched the thief's house, every drawer and chair rung, and found nothing. Dupin listens, and asks a different question.

title: The Gold-Bug
author: Edgar Allan Poe
blurb: A golden beetle, a dirty scrap of parchment and a friend who suddenly stops talking. William Legrand has found something on that paper and will not say what. Weeks later he orders spades and calls his friend to a hill at night.

title: The Wisdom of Father Brown
author: G. K. Chesterton
blurb: A famous scientist is sure the criminal is a tall, bald man named Mr Glass. Father Brown, a short priest with a clumsy umbrella, knows no such man exists. In four stories, clever men build theories and he asks one plain question.

title: The Leavenworth Case
author: Anna Katharine Green
blurb: Horatio Leavenworth is shot dead in his library, and the door key is missing. A stained handkerchief, a key in the ashes and a wall of silence point to Eleanore, the niece a young lawyer is falling for.

title: The Last Train to Harrow Bay
author: Murder on the Orient Express
blurb: Every passenger in Carriage C got the same letter, inviting them aboard the last train of winter. By ten o'clock the man who wrote it has locked his door. By morning he is dead. Young guard Ada Penrose must find out why.

title: The Invisible Man
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: When the clockmender glances at the bandaged stranger's face, he sees a dark hollow where a face should be. Soon a whole village fears a man nobody can see, and only one old classmate, Dr Kemp, might stop him.

title: The Island of Doctor Moreau
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: Edward Prendick is half dead from thirst when a ship picks him up, and its cargo is strange: caged animals and a silent servant. The last stop is an island where a doctor works in secret, and creatures chant strange rules.

title: The First Men in the Moon
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: Broke and trying to write a play, Mr Bedford meets his neighbour Cavor, who has made a metal that blocks gravity. Soon they are flying to the Moon, where insect-like beings live below ground and their ruler wants to know about Earth.

title: Through the Looking-Glass
author: Lewis Carroll
blurb: Behind the mirror over the fireplace, the room looks like Alice's own, but everything is backwards. She steps through into a country laid out like a giant chessboard. If she can cross it, she will become a Queen.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
blurb: Jacob Marley has been dead for seven years, but tonight his ghost walks through Ebenezer Scrooge's door, dragging a heavy chain. He brings a warning. Three spirits will follow, and the last will show Scrooge something he cannot bear to see.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
blurb: The portrait is finished, and Dorian Gray makes a careless wish: let the picture grow old instead of him. Years pass and his face stays smooth. In a locked room at the top of his house, the painting is changing.

title: The Sleeper Awakes
author: H. G. Wells
blurb: Graham has not slept for days. Then he sleeps for 203 years. He wakes in a city of moving roads, where crowds cheer him as master of half the world. But the crowds want something, and so does the Boss.

title: The Dragon Who Lost Her Fire
author: Eragon
blurb: At dusk the dragon Vessa breathes out to light the harbour beacon, and only smoke comes. A boy named Tam helps her climb a snowy pass to find her fire. A storm is coming, and someone wants the light to stay dark.

title: Self-Help
author: Samuel Smiles
blurb: A potter burns his furniture to feed his kiln. A poor barber builds a spinning machine. A man who could not read until about eighteen builds the Rocket. Samuel Smiles gathers their true stories to show what a determined person can do.

title: Character
author: Samuel Smiles
blurb: In 1852 the troopship Birkenhead sinks off South Africa, and the soldiers stand in ranks while women and children leave in the boats. Samuel Smiles uses true stories like this to show what character is made of and how to build it.

title: Walden
author: Henry David Thoreau
blurb: A cabin ten feet by fifteen, three chairs, a field of beans and a quiet pond. Henry David Thoreau moved in on 4 July 1845 to find out how little a person needs, and how much a single day can hold.

title: Habits Over Hype
author: Atomic Habits
blurb: Every January Noor makes big promises, and every year they fade like a wave. This time she tries one thing so small it feels silly, a ten-minute walk after her morning tea. By December, she knows why small beats loud.

title: The Calm Decision
author: Thinking, Fast and Slow
blurb: The email offers Mira a job in another city. She has two days to answer, and her heart says yes before she finishes reading. Her friend Lena tells a sad story about a move gone wrong. Can Mira trust that first feeling?

title: Ten Minutes to Brave
author: Daring Greatly
blurb: In the Thursday team meeting, Priya's hand goes halfway up and stays there. Then she lists small scary things, from saying hello to a neighbour to showing her secret drawings, and meets them one at a time, ten minutes each.

title: The Wealth of Nations
author: Adam Smith
blurb: One man working alone could scarcely make a single pin in a day. Ten men sharing the work made over 48,000. In 1776 Adam Smith used this small workshop to ask why some nations grow rich and others stay poor.

title: The Art of Money Getting
author: P. T. Barnum
blurb: Showman P. T. Barnum made a fortune, lost nearly all of it when a clock company failed, and began again. At seventy he wrote down his golden rules: choose the right work, avoid debt, advertise and keep your good name.

title: The Gospel of Wealth
author: Andrew Carnegie
blurb: Andrew Carnegie, a poor weaver's son who became one of the richest men in America, wrote that a man who dies holding great wealth dies disgraced. His 1889 essay asks what the rich owe everyone else, and it is still argued over.

title: Advice to a Young Tradesman
author: Benjamin Franklin
blurb: Time is money, writes an older printer to a young man about to open his first shop, and he does the sums to prove it. Benjamin Franklin also explains why a good name is worth more than cash.

title: The Principles of Scientific Management
author: Frederick W. Taylor
blurb: About seventy-five men loaded twelve tons of pig iron a day each. One man, with a stop-watch and planned rests, loaded more than forty-seven. Frederick W. Taylor's 1911 book started an argument that never ended. Read it and judge.

title: Your First Hundred Customers
author: The Lean Startup
blurb: Maya mends bicycles, and she has an idea: do it at people's offices while they work. But an idea is only a guess. Follow her from one customer towards a hundred as she asks real questions, listens and counts what matters.

title: The Pricing Puzzle
author: Predictably Irrational
blurb: Ines is never sure about the prices on her Saturday plant stall. Her sixteen-year-old nephew Theo, who studies psychology, says a price is also a message. For a year they test how shoppers judge a price, and they keep it honest.

title: Make It Boring, Make It Rich
author: The Simple Path to Wealth
blurb: A hot tip from a friend, or a dull plan from a retired bus driver? Dara is twenty-seven, has 3,000 dollars saved, and must choose. Uncle Femi's plan is all low fees, cushions and patience, and nothing exciting.

title: The Imitation of Christ
author: Thomas à Kempis
blurb: A fifteenth-century monk writes by candlelight in a stone cell, and his plain advice is still read after more than five hundred years. Thomas a Kempis, in this Christian classic, speaks of humility, inner peace and patience, and of friendship with Christ.

title: Letters from a Stoic
author: Seneca
blurb: A Roman statesman tells a younger friend that the only thing we truly own is time, and most of us give it away. The letters of Seneca on fear, grief, friendship and death read like warm, sharp advice from across the table.

title: The Upanishads
author: Hindu scripture (traditional)
blurb: A boy knocks at the house of Death and will not leave without an answer. In the Upanishads, the great dialogues of ancient India, students ask what the mind is, what happens after death, and who we really are.

title: The Book of Psalms
author: Hebrew Bible
blurb: A shepherd walks through a dark valley, exiles weep beside a river, a deer longs for water. The Book of Psalms gathers 150 ancient songs of joy, fear, doubt and trust, honest about every mood a person can have.

title: The Book of Job
author: Hebrew Bible
blurb: In one day Job loses his herds, his servants and his children, and he did nothing wrong. Three friends come to comfort him, then to argue. The Book of Job asks why good people suffer, and a voice speaks from a whirlwind.

title: The Little Flowers of Saint Francis
author: Franciscan tradition
blurb: A wolf terrifies the town of Gubbio, and one unarmed friar walks out alone to talk to it. This is Francis of Assisi, in stories told about him: a sermon to the birds, and a night of perfect joy in the snow.

title: The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam
author: Omar Khayyam
blurb: A Persian astronomer who measured the stars wrote four-line poems about how short our time is. Omar Khayyam's verses, made famous in English by Edward FitzGerald, ask how to live well with doubt, wine and roses and no sure answers.

title: The Gentle Pilgrim
author: The Alchemist
blurb: Nara has made a hundred clay cups and still does not know what she is for. She sets out for the Quiet Bell on a far mountain. A ferryman, a salt seller and a weaver each teach her something on the way.

title: The Art of Living Long
author: Luigi Cornaro
blurb: At forty, a rich Venetian was often ill, and his doctors warned him to change his life. He began to weigh his food and wine, and says he was well within a year. Read his story, and what science makes of it.

title: Move a Little Every Hour
author: Spark
blurb: Nadia works on the fourth floor and is stiff, tired and slow. This week she tries one small change, a little movement every hour, and her colleague Tom joins in. Learn what long sitting does and how little it takes to begin.

title: Stretch for Ten Minutes
author: Becoming Flexible
blurb: One January morning, a taxi driver cannot tie his own shoes because his back will not bend. Dev joins a free ten-minute stretching class, and over twelve weeks learns what flexibility is, what the evidence says and how to begin gently.

title: Strong Bones for Life
author: Strong Women, Strong Bones
blurb: Joan, seventy-four, slips on a wet garden step and breaks her wrist. Her daughter Tess learns that bones are alive and always rebuilding. Over one year the family looks at the food, movement and balance that help look after the skeleton.

title: Water, Simply
author: Your Body's Many Cries for Water
blurb: What does water do? Ben, a bicycle courier, asks after a dizzy July afternoon, and his grandmother Nell, who barely drinks, makes the question matter. He learns how thirst works, how much is enough and which myths to drop.

title: Healthy Habits for a Busy Family
author: Atomic Habits
blurb: Nadia writes twelve new rules to fix her family's whole life, and by Friday nobody has kept one. Then a retired nurse next door says to start much smaller. A glass of water at breakfast is where one busy family begins.

title: Heart Health in Plain Words
author: The Heart Health Handbook
blurb: When his brother Karl has a heart attack, baker Walter knows nothing about his own heart. Over six Thursday evenings, a cardiac nurse explains the pump, the pipes and the risks in plain words, and which ones small changes can lower.

title: Eyes, Screens and Rest
author: The Myopia Myth
blurb: Burning eyes after a day at two screens, and a son who squints at the school board. Lena, an illustrator, visits a kind optometrist who explains how eyes work, what screens do and do not do, and which everyday habits can help.

title: History of the Peloponnesian War
author: Thucydides
blurb: A plague strikes Athens, a city packed with people who fled the enemy army, and one of the sick writes down all he sees. Thucydides records most of a long war with Sparta, from great speeches to a doomed fleet at Syracuse.

title: The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
author: Edward Gibbon
blurb: In 1764 a young Englishman sat among the ruins of Rome, listened to friars singing on the Capitol, and decided to learn how it all fell. Edward Gibbon follows the story for over a thousand years, to the fall of Constantinople.

title: Common Sense
author: Thomas Paine
blurb: The pamphlet names no author, only an Englishman. In January 1776 it reaches a country at war but mostly still loyal to its king. Thomas Paine uses plain words to ask why a small island should rule a whole continent forever.

title: A Journal of the Plague Year
author: Daniel Defoe
blurb: While the roads out of London fill with people fleeing the plague, saddler HF opens his Bible and decides to stay. In 1665 he sees red crosses on doors, silent streets, great pits and neighbours who risk their lives to help.

title: The Diary of Samuel Pepys
author: Samuel Pepys
blurb: A maid wakes Samuel Pepys at three in the morning to report a fire in the City. He goes back to bed. Two days later he buries wine and a cheese in his garden. His secret diary holds a stormy marriage too.

title: The Silk Road in Ten Stops
author: The Silk Roads
blurb: Around 1900 a man finds a sealed cave holding tens of thousands of manuscripts. It is one of ten stops, from Chang'an to Venice, on a road that was never one road. Meet the traders and monks who carried silk and paper.

title: How the Printing Press Changed Everything
author: The Gutenberg Revolution
blurb: About 1450 Johannes Gutenberg borrowed 800 guilders from a rich merchant to build an idea, metal letters used again and again. A few years later the merchant took him to court. Follow the press from that workshop to the screens of today.

title: Eleven Days That Changed the World
author: Sapiens
blurb: A student in Los Angeles tries to log in to a computer 560 kilometres away, and it crashes after two letters. That evening in 1969 is one of eleven dated days, from Columbus to Gagarin, that each opened a door to change.

title: The Descent of Man
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: In his famous book of 1859, Charles Darwin said almost nothing about human beings. In 1871 he turned his evidence on us, from tailbones and unborn babies to peacocks and bowerbirds. This retelling also says plainly where he was wrong.

title: The Sidereal Messenger
author: Galileo Galilei
blurb: On 7 January 1610, Galileo saw three small stars in a line beside Jupiter. Four days later he knew they were circling it. His short book tells the story and adds mountains on the Moon and a sky full of new stars.

title: Micrographia
author: Robert Hooke
blurb: Samuel Pepys stayed up until two in the morning reading a book of drawings of fleas, a fly's eye and cork. In 1665 Robert Hooke drew what he saw through a microscope, and he gave the cell its name.

title: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals
author: Charles Darwin
blurb: Charles Darwin pressed his face to the glass beside a puff adder to test himself. The snake struck, and he jumped back anyway. His 1872 book uses faces, animals and babies to show that feelings carry marks of a long past.

title: The Secret Life of the Ocean
author: The Blue Planet
blurb: Every night, the largest migration on Earth rises through the dark sea to feed, then sinks again by day. Sink through glowing fish and hot vents to the deepest trench, and see why this world needs our care.

title: How Your Brain Learns
author: Make It Stick
blurb: Rereading your notes feels like learning, but it gives only a false feeling of knowing. Ana finds that out the hard way, and her neighbour, a retired teacher, shows her what works better, from testing herself to spacing and sleep.

title: The Weather in Plain Words
author: The Weather Book
blurb: A raindrop is not shaped like a tear, and it takes about a million cloud drops to make one. Follow the sun's heat through wind, clouds, fronts and storms, in plain words, and learn to read the sky for yourself.

title: A Short History of Medicine
author: The Emperor of All Maladies
blurb: In 1854 John Snow marked cholera deaths on a street map and traced them to one water pump. This short history follows people's fight against disease, from the first healers to vaccines and scans, through bad ideas and brave ones.
